column2: The get of Vlad von Carstein, the bloodline that would rule the living as a lord rules his serfs. The Court of Sylvania hides behind the masks of mortal nobility until the night it is ready to march, and then the dead march with it. Its masters prize strength, cunning and the patience to wait out the centuries.
The Master of Court commands every von Carstein, and in the end the dead of Sylvania themselves.

The knightly order of the Blood Dragons, founded in the Blood Keep by Walach Harkon. Abhorash taught that the curse is mastered by perfection in battle, and his get seek that perfection through duel and quest, scorning the schemes of lesser bloodlines. Honour is everything to a Blood Dragon, and a knight who loses it is cast back down among the squires.
The Grand Master of the Ordo Draconis leads the knights of the Blood Keep and judges every challenge.

The daughters of Neferata, Queen of Lahmia. The Sisters rule from behind thrones, in the beds and ears of princes, and few mortals ever learn that the beautiful woman at court is centuries dead. From the Silver Pinnacle the Queen of Mysteries spins a web that reaches every court of the Old World.
The Queen of Mysteries is the voice of Neferata, and every Sister owes her obedience and favour.

The heirs of W'soran, scholars of death who care nothing for the world of the living except as material. In their towers they labour for centuries over a single work, and their greatest dream is to finish what Nagash began. A Necrarch is judged by what they have learned, and by what they have made.
The Lords of the Dark Tower are the greatest minds of the bloodline, and W'soran is first among them.

The cursed descendants of Ushoran, last king of Strygos, whose realm the orcs and the Nagashi threw down. The Strigoi are outcasts, hated by the other bloodlines and hunted by the living, and they live among graveyards with their ghoul courts. Yet they remember that they were once kings, and some dream of Strygos reborn.
The Heir of Ushoran would be the first king of the Strigoi since Strygos fell.

Long ago the Dragon Emperor poisoned the serpent-kin of the east, and they should have died. The Dark Crystals kept them alive instead, and changed them into what they are now: more snake than man, cold of blood and patient as stone. The Jade Coil is the hidden mirror of Cathay, a court of mandarins and sages who serve nothing but their own hunger and the visions in the crystals.
The Serpent Sage gazes deepest into the Dark Crystals and speaks for the whole Coil.

The Mahtmasi have no kings and no hierarchy, only the eldest and the hungriest. They come when they are called, feeding on those who ask for them, loving and then devouring. They can become a swarm of flies and carrion birds, they eat their own kind, and they fear fire, sunlight and running water. The eldest of them keeps the gate of Gwingui, where the shadow realm touches the world.
The Big Bokor keeps the gate of Gwingui and is the closest thing the Carrion Children have to a master.
Claim a higher place in [Root.Society.GetName]. A vampire rises on deeds, standing and the trial of the bloodline. A living thrall can climb only so far.
Every bloodline tests those who would stand among its masters. Undertake the trial of [Root.Society.GetName].
The thirst never sleeps. Choose your prey.
Ask the Head of the Bloodline for Aid
You are at war, and the head of [Root.Society.GetName] has gold and the dead to spare. Ask for help, though they may refuse.
Your master thirsts. Offer your own veins, and rise in their esteem.
There are places your master cannot go: a temple, a market at noon, a guild hall in the sun. Go in their place.
Your liege is one of the undying. Take the faith of the vampires, swear yourself to their service, and become a thrall.
Has done a deed worthy of the bloodline (fed on worthy prey, answered a plea, served a master, won a duel), or holds the standing the bloodline expects
Is a vampire (living thralls rise no higher)
Is not a hidden von Carstein (throw off the mask first)
Has passed the trial of the bloodline
Is not already undertaking the trial
Has not failed the trial recently
Has not fed in the last two years
Has not asked for aid in the last ten years
The head of the bloodline is someone else, free and able
Has not offered blood in the last three years
Has not run an errand in the last five years
Feeding on the helpless shames a Blood Dragon.
The Mahtmasi feed on those who ask. Taking the unwilling is a poor offering.
A living servant of the undying, bound to a bloodline.
The thirst is quiet for now, and the blood runs strong.
Too much blood given, too little left.
The head of the bloodline has lent the dead of their lands to this war.
Sworn to the service of a vampire.

The court of Sylvania has taken note of you. Your name is spoken now in the halls of Drakenhof, and lesser vampires lower their eyes when you pass. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank] of the von Carstein line.
Before the knights of the Ordo Draconis you kneel and rise again as [Root.GetSocietyRank]. Abhorash taught that the curse is mastered only by perfection of the blade. You have come one step nearer.

A letter on scented paper, sealed in red wax with a serpent and a crown. The Sisters have weighed you and found you useful. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank] now, and the web of the Silver Pinnacle grows a thread tighter around the world.
The Brotherhood does not celebrate. A single page arrives, written in a hand that has not changed in five centuries, acknowledging that your work has merit. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank].

The ghouls howl in the graveyard and the bones are thrown. Among the outcast heirs of Strygos you are [Root.GetSocietyRank] now, and the others will remember it the next time the hunger drives them to your door.
You lay your coils before the Dark Crystal and the visions part to show you your own face, older and colder. The Jade Coil names you [Root.GetSocietyRank].
The Carrion Children have no thrones. But the flies settle on you a little more readily now, and the bokors whisper your name when they make their offerings. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank].

The thirst is upon you. Your servants keep a few souls fed and docile in the cellars for nights like this. But out in the dark there are warriors, hot-blooded and strong, whose blood would sing in your veins for years.

The thirst is upon you. There are servants in the cellars who would offer their necks without a word. Abhorash would call that the feeding of a beast. A Blood Dragon takes blood from those who can fight for it.

The hunger wakes you. Far off, someone has made an offering and spoken your name: a widow who wants a lover, a merchant who wants his rival dead, a mother who wants her child to live. They asked for you. They will have you, and you will have them.
A warrior, taken in the dark.

column1: Your humble [From.GetSocietyRank] is beset. My enemies press upon my lands and I have not the strength to throw them back alone. I beg the aid of our blood, in gold or in the dead of your domain, and I will remember the gift for as long as I walk.

column2: Send the dead of my lands.
Let them stand or fall alone.
A reply from [From.GetTitledName] has come, and with it help. The head of [Root.Society.GetName] has not forgotten their own.
The blood looks after its own.

column1: If you cannot hold your own lands you do not deserve them. Do not write to me again until you have something to offer.

column2: [From.GetTitledFirstName] kneels before you and bares [From.GetHerHis] throat. The thrall offers [From.GetHerHis] blood freely, as a servant should, and the pulse at [From.GetHerHis] neck beats fast.

Your master needs a letter carried into a temple, a debt collected in the market at noon, a priest bribed in his own chapel. These are places where no vampire can go, and so you go instead, smiling in the sun with the mark of the teeth hidden under your collar.
Ride out to challenge a famed mortal champion in single combat. A squire who wins proves themselves worthy of knighthood.
By the custom of the Order any Blood Dragon Lord may challenge the Grand Master before the assembled knights. The victor leads the Ordo Draconis.
The Blood Keep was raised by Walach Harkon as the heart of the Order. Its Grand Master must hold it.
Abhorash mastered the thirst alone on the peaks of the World's Edge, and then vanished. Leave the Blood Keep and follow his trail.
Has not issued a challenge in the last three years
Has not challenged the Grand Master in the last twenty years
Is not already on the trail
Has not set out on the trail in the last twenty-five years
With no Honour left to lose, the code of Abhorash casts you down among the squires!
A victory on the Blood Quest passes the trial of the Order.
You defeat the Grand Master and take the leadership of the Order.
In two or three years you will reach the high peaks.
The beast falls and the trail leads on.
The beast throws you down the mountain. The trail is lost.
Every knight of the Ordo Draconis gains Honour.
Mastered the red thirst after battle, as Abhorash taught.
Dreamed of the founder's long vigil on the peaks.
Dreamed of the founder's wrath in battle.
Stood on the peak where Abhorash conquered the thirst, and learned how it was done.

In the market towns they sing of a mortal champion who has never been unhorsed. You send your herald to name the day. When you ride onto the field at dusk the crowd falls silent, and the champion's hand shakes on his lance.
Steel against steel, as Abhorash taught.
Tear out his throat and be done.

The knights of the Order stand in a ring in the great hall of the Blood Keep. You throw your gauntlet at the feet of [vampsoc_foe.GetTitledName] and speak the old words. [vampsoc_foe.GetSheHe] rises and draws [vampsoc_foe.GetHerHis] blade without a word.
Only one of us will leave this ring as Grand Master.
[From.GetTitledName] stands over you in the ring, and the knights of the Order kneel to [From.GetHerHim]. By the custom of Abhorash the Ordo Draconis is no longer yours.

The knights of the Order gather to strip you of spurs and rank. You have no Honour left to lose, and the code of Abhorash is clear. You will start again among the squires, and earn back what you have thrown away.
A young knight kneels in your hall, sword across his palms. He has heard of the Order and of the Blood Keep, and he begs to serve as your squire until the day he has earned the blood.
Deep in his cups at your feast, a mortal knight laughs and calls the Blood Dragons a pack of leeches in borrowed armour. The hall goes quiet and every eye turns to you.
He is not worth my blade.
The battle is won and the field is red. The dying moan in the mud, and the thirst roars in you like a fire. Abhorash conquered this hunger. Lesser vampires drown in it.
I am the master, not the thirst.
The champion of a rival lord is dead, cut down in a fair fight by your hand. The knights of the Order speak of it with respect, and the tale spreads.
A herald in blood-red livery brings a summons from [vampsoc_head.GetTitledName]. The knights of the Order are to gather at the Blood Keep and prove their skill in the lists.
In the day-sleep you dream of Abhorash, alone on a peak above the clouds, starving himself of blood until he was master of the thirst. Then he turns and looks at you.
You leave the Blood Keep in the hands of your seneschal and ride east towards the World's Edge, where they say Abhorash fought a dragon and drank its blood, and was never thirsty again.
The trail has led you to a cave high in the peaks, and the bones of a hundred knights are scattered around its mouth. Something vast stirs in the dark.

At the top of the world, on a ledge of black stone, you find the place where Abhorash knelt. His sword is gone, but the stone remembers. You kneel where he knelt, and for the first time in centuries the thirst falls quiet.
The seal of the Court of Sylvania, carried by its envoys. Mortal lords who see it know who they are dealing with.
Blood-red plate forged in the Blood Keep for a knight of the Ordo Draconis.
A portrait of the Queen of Mysteries carved in black stone. Mortals find it hard to refuse its wearer.
A copied fragment of the great work of Nagash. The ink has never quite dried.
A crown of old gold and finger bones, dug from the ruins of Ushoran's kingdom.
A sliver of the crystals that keep the Jade Coil alive. Visions move in its depths.
A bundle of feathers, teeth and a dried heart, offered at the gate of Gwingui.
Take the Tithe of the Houses
Every Lahmian house owes the Queen of Mysteries a share of what it takes from the living, and so does every mortal caught in the web.
The world knows what you are. Leave it behind: a new name, a new face, a new court, and the old rumours die with your old life.
The Silver Pinnacle in the World's Edge is the seat of Neferata and the heart of the Sisterhood. Its Queen must hold it.
From the Silver Pinnacle, bind every court of the Old World to the Sisterhood with letters, lovers and debts.
This mortal ruler is at war. Send gold or sellswords, and they will owe you more than they know.
Has not taken the tithe in the last five years
Has not drawn the veil in the last thirty years
Has not assisted a mortal in the last three years
Is not already spinning the web
Every Lahmian ruler pays 50 gold, and every Lahmian house and mortal in the web pays 25 gold.
In three to five years the web will be spun.
A mission that pays off passes the trial of the Sisterhood.
You are exposed as a vampire!
You turn her whispers against her.
She has the Queen's ear, not you.
Away from court until the talk dies down.
The courts of the Old World answer to the Silver Pinnacle, though few of them know it.

[vampsoc_mortal.GetTitledName] is at war and losing. A word from you, a chest of gold or a company of sellswords under a borrowed banner, and [vampsoc_mortal.GetSheHe] will be grateful for the rest of [vampsoc_mortal.GetHerHis] short life.
On second thought, let them fall.
The letters come from every court of the Old World, each sealed with the serpent and the crown, each with its tithe. The Houses of Lahmia remember who rules them.
A witch hunter has come to court asking questions about the beautiful lady who is never seen at mass, never seen by day, and never seems to eat. He has not yet said your name aloud. He will soon.
He will not leave the city alive.
Leave court until he loses interest.
One of your Sisters has been whispering against you in the ear of the Queen of Mysteries, claiming your missions fail and your houses are poorly run. Lahmians do not forgive such things.
A letter from the Silver Pinnacle, in [vampsoc_head.GetTitledFirstName]'s own hand. A cardinal in a distant court needs to be bought, and the Queen has decided that you will pay for him.
Let her find the gold elsewhere.
A young knight of the court has been following you for weeks, pale and lovesick. Tonight he kneels and begs to give you his blood, if only you will let him touch your hand.
Let him beg in front of everyone.

You host a masked ball, and the lords and princes of the realm come in silk and velvet. They dance with you until dawn and tell you every secret they have, and in the morning they remember none of it.
A courtier has found a portrait of you in an old gallery, painted sixty years ago, and you have not aged a day. Now [Root.GetHerHis] servants whisper about it in the kitchens.
Buy the portrait and the courtier.
The courtier will not see another night.
Let them talk. Who would believe it?

From the Silver Pinnacle you send your daughters out into every court of the Old World with letters, gifts and orders. It will take years, but when it is done there will be no throne that does not answer to you.

The web is spun. Emperors and kings sleep beside your daughters, bishops owe you their mitres and the merchant princes of Marienburg keep your secrets. The Old World does not know it, but it is yours.
As Lahmia ruled, so shall I.
Enough hiding. Show your court what you are, and let them fear you as they should. The mask cannot be put back on.
Call the dead of your lands from their graves to fight in this war. They will crumble back to dust at the peace.
Call up the Grave Guard, dead knights in black armour who serve the Court of Sylvania for one more war.
Summon the Counts of the Court to Drakenhof for a night of blood and politics. They will leave richer and more loyal.
The Master of Court should rule Sylvania itself.
Work the great ritual over the land of Sylvania, binding its dead and its soil to you forever.
Has not raised the dead in the last five years
Has not summoned the Grave Guard in the last ten years
Has not held a night court in the last five years
Is not already working the ritual
A host of 1000 dead rises at your capital, until the peace.
400 Grave Guard and 50 Vampire Knights rise at your capital, until the peace.
Every member of the Court gains Blood and thinks better of you.
In two or three years the ritual will be done.
Every county of Sylvania held by you or your vassals is bound to the dead.
You have passed the trial of your bloodline.
You have failed the trial, and must wait five years to try again.
Threw off the mask. The court has not forgotten what it saw.
The dead of a village graveyard march with the levies.
The Counts of Sylvania have feasted at this vampire's table.
With Vlad gone, this Vampire Lord would be master of Sylvania.
The land of Sylvania is bound to this vampire, and its dead rise at their call.
The dead of this land answer the Master of Court.

The trial of the Court is the Night of Blood: one night to raise the dead of a graveyard and drown a village in terror, and be gone before dawn, unseen. The village of a rival lord would make the Court take notice. A village of your own is safer.
A rival's village. Let them all see.
One of my own villages, quietly.
By dawn the village is silent and the dead are back in their graves. No one saw you come or go. When word reaches Drakenhof, the Court will know you are worthy.
The dead would not rise, or rose too slowly, and the villagers fled with torches. The Court of Sylvania will hear of your failure.
The Court will know my name.
You stand before your court and let them see you as you are: the teeth, the eyes, the stillness of the dead. Some faint, some pray, and some fall to their knees. None of them will ever forget.

[From.GetTitledName] is dead, truly dead, and the Ring could not save [From.GetHerHim]. The Court of Sylvania has lost its master, and every Vampire Lord in Sylvania is already looking at the others with hungry eyes.
The Court needs a new master.
Twenty years of feuding, betrayals and murder are over. The Counts of Sylvania have bent the knee, some willingly, some not. You are the Master of Court, and no one will question it again.
[vampsoc_rival.GetTitledName] holds lands you could take while the Feud rages. Or [vampsoc_rival.GetSheHe] could be useful against the others, for now.
An alliance, until it suits me to end it.
One of the lesser vampires of the Court has been courting your vassals and eyeing your lands. He thinks you have grown soft.
Humble him in front of the Court.
The dead in a village graveyard have begun to stir on their own, scratching at their coffins and moaning in the night. They can feel you in the land.
The court chaplain has noticed that you never take the sacrament, never stand in the sun, and that your reflection is faint in the chapel glass. He has started to write letters.
A letter sealed in black wax: [vampsoc_head.GetTitledFirstName] demands tribute from every Count of the Court.
Let the Master come and take it.
A young noble of your court comes to you at midnight and begs to be made one of the undying. He offers you anything, his lands, his family, his blood.
Perhaps, one day. Start with your blood.
Your envoy has come back from a mortal court with a treaty, and with stories about how the mortal lords trembled to see the seal of Drakenhof.
You stand on the highest tower of your castle and begin the ritual. It will take years. When it is done, every grave in Sylvania will answer to you, and the soil itself will remember your name.
The ritual is done. Mist rolls over the hills of Sylvania, the graveyards stir, and the peasants bar their doors at dusk. The land belongs to the dead, and the dead belong to you.
Send an expedition into the deserts of Nehekhara to find a relic of the Great Necromancer: a bone, a page, a shard of his crown.
Take a Seat in the Dark Tower
With a relic of Nagash in hand, claim one of the three seats of the Lords of the Dark Tower.
Bind the spirit of a dead champion back into his bones. He will lead your armies without rest and without complaint.
W'soran taught that Nagash left a recipe for the mastery of death. With the relic and the lore of centuries, you can rebuild it.
Teach this courtier the dark arts. The teaching sharpens your own mind as much as theirs.
Has not sent an expedition in the last five years
Has not raised a wight in the last fifteen years
Is not already working on the recipe
You have a relic of Nagash. A seat in the Dark Tower is within reach.
In three to five years the recipe will be complete.
Completed a great work on the flesh of the dead.
Completed a great work on the binding of souls.
Completed a great work on the Winds of Magic and the stars.
A dead champion, bound back into his bones.
A breakthrough has mended the decay of centuries, for a while.
Studying the dark arts under a Necrarch.
A tower of laboratories, ossuaries and libraries.
The graveyards of this province have been emptied.
The peasants fear the tower's lights.
Has rebuilt the Great Necromancer's mastery of death.
The trial of the Brotherhood is the Magnum Opus: a single great work that will take years of your unlife. What will you study?
The Winds of Magic and the stars.
After years in the dark, the work is finished. You send a copy to the Dark Tower. The answer comes back in a single line: the Brotherhood acknowledges your work.
The work has collapsed: a false premise in the third volume, an error copied from a corrupt text. Years wasted. You will have to start again.
You hire grave robbers, desperate scholars and a few thralls to lead them, and send them south into the Land of the Dead to look for a relic of Nagash.
The expedition comes back half-dead, but with a bundle wrapped in rotten linen. Inside is a finger bone, black as obsidian, that hums with power. A relic of Nagash.
The Tomb Kings caught the expedition in the desert. A few survivors stagger home to tell of skeleton chariots and the wrath of the dead kings.
The expedition comes back empty-handed, with a few scrolls and tales of sand.
You have opened the barrow of an ancient champion and called his spirit back into his bones. Now he stands before you in rusted armour, eyes burning cold, waiting for your command.
After years of labour, it comes to you in one night: the missing piece, the answer to a question you have been asking for decades.
Send the work to the Tower.
Use it on my own decaying body.
A Necrarch of the Brotherhood has written forty pages disputing a point in your last treatise. The tone is insulting.
I have better things to do.
Your apprentice, [vampsoc_apprentice.GetFirstName], has been working alone in the laboratory while you slept.
Let us see what [vampsoc_apprentice.GetSheHe] has done.
Your work needs fresh bodies, and the cellars are empty.
Buy them from across the border.
Your tower is too small for your work. A new floor would hold a laboratory, an ossuary and a library.
In a forgotten chest you find notes in your own hand from three centuries ago, and they are better than you remembered.
The peasants complain that the lights in the tower burn all night, that strange smells drift on the wind, and that their dead do not stay in their graves.
Give them some coin and send them home.
With the relic of Nagash before you and the notes of centuries, you begin the work that W'soran dreamed of: the Recipe for Nagash.
It is done. You hold the Recipe for Nagash, and with it a mastery of death that no Necrarch has had since W'soran himself.
Call the ghouls up from the crypts and set them on your enemies. They will slink back to the graves at the peace.
The Heir of Ushoran calls the scattered children of Strygos home.
Rebuild the court of Ushoran, and make the Strigoi kings again.
Has not loosed the ghouls in the last five years
Has not called the Strigoi home in the last ten years
800 ghouls and 100 crypt horrors rise at your capital, until the peace.
Every Strigoi gains Hunger, and landless Strigoi come to your court.
In three or four years the court of Ushoran will stand again.
Every Strigoi gains Hunger and thinks better of you.
In the frenzy, someone at court dies.
A court of ghouls follows this Strigoi.
A large and unruly court of ghouls follows this Strigoi.
Holding back the curse of Ushoran by will alone.
Remembers the marble halls of Strygos.
Remembers the fall of Strygos, and the hunger after.
The court of Ushoran stands again.

The trial of the Strigoi is the ghoul court. Every Strigoi lord is followed by ghouls, the cannibal wretches who live among the graves. You must gather your own. The starving poor would make a large court, if you can hold them. The graveyard-eaters already know what they are.
They come to you on all fours out of the graveyards, gnawing bones and howling your name. You have a court.
The ghouls scattered, or turned on each other, or were burned by the villagers. You have no court.
You have gone too long without blood, and the curse of Ushoran claws at you. Your face twists, your nails grow into claws, and you can smell the blood of every servant in the castle.
Chain yourself in the crypt until it passes.
A vampire of another bloodline has called the Strigoi beasts and grave-eaters before witnesses, and laughed while saying it.
A Strigany caravan comes in the night, with news from the roads, stolen goods and a cart of volunteers who have sworn themselves to the old blood.
Take the goods and the news.
The ghouls have dug up a fresh graveyard and the crypt reeks of their feast. They watch you, waiting to see if you will join them.
In the day-sleep you walk the marble halls of Strygos before it fell. Ushoran sits on his throne, beautiful and terrible, and he asks what you will do with his legacy.
Your servants have been digging in the ruins of a Strygan city, and they bring up old gold and broken things.
Vampire hunters have tracked you to your lair. They have stakes, fire and a priest.
You send word to every Strigoi lord and every Strigany caravan: the Heir of Ushoran is calling the children of Strygos home, to build the court again.
They have come, from the graveyards and the mountains and the roads. The court of Ushoran stands again, and its king sits on the throne of Strygos.
The examination of the Coil is a cruel mirror of the Imperial examinations of Cathay: three days of questions put by the Serpent Sage's serpents. Those who pass are marked as the Sage's heirs.
Coil in the dark of the crystal chamber and shed the old skin, and the jade decay with it.
Fill your court with mandarins, scribes and serpents, all of them bound to the crystal and to you.
Coil around the greatest of the Dark Crystals and gaze at the whole of the heavens. The Dragon Throne is not your concern. Everything under it is.
Wind this mortal ruler in the coils of the Jade Court. They will pay tribute now, and find it hard to refuse you later.
Has not sat the examination in the last ten years
Has not shed the skin in the last fifteen years
Has not held a crystal court in the last ten years
Has not used the Serpent's Coils in the last five years
You pass the examination. The Coil marks you as the Sage's heir.
A true vision in the crystal passes the trial of the Jade Coil.
Someone at the capital wonders where the scribe went.
In three or four years you will have seen everything.
Fresh scales after shedding the old skin.
Basking by the light of the Dark Crystal.
Mandarins, scribes and serpents run the realm.
Fascinated by a serpent of the Jade Court.
Has seen the whole of the heavens in the Dark Crystal.

For three days and three nights you lie coiled before the Serpent Sage's servants, answering questions on the poisons of the east, the ledgers of the Celestial Bureaucracy, the movements of the stars and the taste of an Imperial Scribe's blood.
You coil in the dark of the crystal chamber and feel the old skin split along your spine. It comes away whole, grey and brittle, and the jade decay comes away with it.
A serpent's eyes meet yours across the hall of [From.GetTitledName], and you cannot look away. When at last you can, you have promised tribute, and you are not sorry.
An Imperial Scribe has arrived to count the taxes of your province, with his brushes, his ledgers and his soft, inky throat. The Jade Coil has always found scribes delicious.
Bribe him to leave and keep the ledgers clean.
The old skin grows tight and itches beneath the scales. It is not yet time to shed, but the crystal's light would ease it.
The Dark Crystal hums in the night, and shapes move in its depths.
Another Jade vampire has been trying to hypnotise your servants and steal them away. You meet in the crystal chamber, and neither of you blinks.
A servant brings you a sliver of dark crystal found in a mountain stream, still warm to the touch.
Agents of the Dragon Emperor are hunting the serpent-kin again, as they have since the poison. They have fire, jade swords and the Emperor's own seal.
You coil around the greatest of the Dark Crystals and look into it, past the visions, past the dreams, into the heavens themselves.
You have seen everything under heaven: every province, every throne, every serpent and every scribe. The Dragon Emperor sits on his throne, and you know all he does not.
The heavens are mine to see.
Go to the gate of Gwingui, where the shadow realm touches the world, and keep vigil until the gate decides what you are.
Open the gate of Gwingui and let the shadow host pour out into the world, for one war.
The Westerlanders took Sudenburg and brought the witch hunters of Samur with them. Claim it back.
Turn the shadow realm against the Westerlanders of Sudenburg and the witch hunters of Samur, until not one of them sleeps easy.
This vampire sits in your dungeon. The Carrion Children eat their own kind.
Send this mortal a dream of longing, or of terror.
Has not kept vigil in the last ten years
Has not opened the gate in the last ten years
Has not sent a dream in the last three years
Has not devoured kin in the last ten years
Is not already casting them out
1200 shadow-touched warriors and 300 archers pour out at your capital, until the peace.
The gate accepts you. You are marked as the next keeper.
In two or three years the shadows will take Sudenburg.
Every Mahtmasi gains Offerings, and the lands of Sudenburg you hold are haunted for good.
A year of love before the end.
Has eaten another vampire, as the Carrion Children do.
Wakes screaming from dreams of flies and carrion birds.
Has drifted over the land as flies and carrion birds, hearing everything.
Taught in dreams by the first of the Mahtmasi.
The villagers burned the shrine of the Carrion Children.
Cast the Westerlanders out of Sudenburg.
The shadow realm lies close here, and the living leave offerings at every door.
